stem:
A $0.17\text{ g}$ sample of a Group 14 chloride, $\text{XCl}_4$, reacted with water to produce an oxide, $\text{XO}_2$, and $\text{HCl}$.

equation 1 $$\text{XCl}_4(\text{s}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \rightarrow \text{XO}_2(\text{s}) + 4\text{HCl}(\text{aq})$$

The $\text{HCl}$ produced was absorbed in $100\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sodium hydroxide solution (an excess).

In a titration, the unreacted sodium hydroxide solution required $30.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.20\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ hydrochloric acid for complete neutralisation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of hydrochloric acid used in the titration to neutralise the unreacted sodium hydroxide solution.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of sodium hydroxide neutralised in the titration.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of sodium hydroxide that reacted with the $\text{HCl}$ produced by the reaction in equation 1.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of $\text{HCl}$ produced by the reaction in equation 1.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of $\text{XCl}_4$ in the original $0.17\text{ g}$ sample.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text: Calculate the relative atomic mass, $A_r$, of $\text{X}$ and suggest its identity.
